Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Gameplay 4 Round Scoring 5 Game End Overview CATsle Builders is a trick taking game for 👤 3 players to 👤 5 players players. It's played with a deck of 60 cards divided into 5 Suits with Values ranging from 1 to 12. The 5 Suits are Walls (white), Gables (green), Gates (red), Bridges (yellow), and Moats (blue). The game consists of 3 Rounds , in each of which players aim to fill their players areas with a number of cards without surpassing the respective card limit . Setup Each round is set up identically, with each player being dealt a hand of cards depending on the player count. In a 👤 3 players player game, the 12 Moat cards are removed from the deck and are not used. Player count Deck size Hand size 3 48 11 4 60 14 5 60 12 In the 1st Round, the first player is selected randomly, and each subsequent Round starts with the player next in turn order after the previous Round's first player. The order of play will always be clockwise. Gameplay A round consists of a sequence of tricks played until all players are out of cards in their hands. During each trick, players choose one card from their hand to play. The first player can play any card from their hand. Then, every other player must play a card of the same suit as the first player. After each player has played a card, the players' rating is determined by comparing the cards' Suits and Values . The leading Suit beats all other Suits, and higher Values beat lower Values. When comparing two cards of non-leading Suit and same Values, the card player later in the trick is stronger. After the rating is determined, staring from the highest rank, a number of players take 1 or 2 cards from the trick. The number of cards taken is affected by the player count. Finally in a 👤 4 players + player game, everyone's boards include an additional column with a limit of 0. Player count 1st rating cards 2nd rating cards 3rd rating cards 3 1 2 - 4 1 2 - 5 1 1 2 When a player takes a card, it must be added to one of the 4 columns under the player's board. If there is already a card of the same Suit in one of the columns, the new card must be added to the same column. Otherwise, it can be placed in any of the empty columns. If you can avoid going over the limit you will score the cards in the column. Each column has a limit of cards that can be added to it without receiving a penalty. The penalty happens when you add a card exceeding that column's limit. The played card (or cards) are turned sideways when added to a column. Every sideways card will subtract from your score. After all required cards are taken, the next trick starts with the player who took 2 cards in the current trick. If this was the last trick of the round, the game proceeds to scoring. Round Scoring The score gained by players after each round is determined by the number of cards in each of their board's columns. It's gained/lost from these 3 sources: ⚒ If the number of cards in a column is within the limit , the score from that column equals to the number of cards in it ⚒ If the number of cards in a column is above the limit , the score from that column equals to the negative number of sideways cards in it ⚒ Additionally, the perfect score bonus is awarded according to the number of columns in which the number of cards is exactly equal to the limit (except that column 0 is never considered perfect) Number of perfect columns 0 1 2 3 4 Bonus score 0 0 1 2 4 The resulting round score is the sum of all these scores. [Rating: 3/10] No control at all, especially if you get a bunch of middle cards. But you can want no more cards and get 3rd place with a 1. That gives you 2 cards and negative points!!!  Dumb, dumb, dumb.

[Rating: 4/10] Can't remember much about this game, but I remember not enjoying it. Played at Bordercon 2025

[Rating: 5/10] There doesn't seem to be a lot going on here except to try to delay taking tricks for as long as possible.

[Rating: 5/10] A trick taking game where players play must follow tricks, highest value picks 1 card played into their tableau (1/2/3/4 card columns where like colored cards share the same column), 2 second player must gain 2 cards played, and the last player gains nothing (3p). The 2nd player leads the trick. When all players play their cards, scoring is based on players who are either meet or under their column restrictions - 1/2/3/4, and losing a point if they exceed the limit of each column. After 3 rounds, the player with most points wins.

[Rating: 5/10] Played on BGA. Trick taker where you're only trying to take so many of each suit. It's mildly interesting, but after playing a single round of the game I was ready for it to be over.  Cute art though.

[Rating: 5/10] After 1 play on BGA: There are quite a few trick-taking games where the goal is to win just the right amount of tricks. A big part of the challenge is assessing your own cards in relation to what the other players are likely holding. With this game, though, I felt like I had less control over how things played out than I do in a classic like Skull King. I also found it rather punishing that my fortunes can be hanging by a thread at several points. For example, finishing second means I have to draw two cards, which can really hurt. Thankfully, the theming has absolutely nothing to do with the game. The deck comes in five suits numbered 1-12 with no trump or special cards. It is a follow suit game with the highest card in the original suit winning.
